compliances.name: Report new hires to South Carolina
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: South Carolina Department of Social Services (State Directory of New Hires)
compliances.brief: An employer who hires, or rehires after at least 60 days away, an employee who lives or works in South Carolina reports the hire to the state directory of new hires. The report can be the W-4 form or an equivalent.
compliances.why: You have employees in South Carolina.

due.text: Within 20 calendar days of hiring each employee

compliances.dueText: Within twenty calendar days of the hiring of the employee. Employers who report electronically send reports twice a month, not less than 12 nor more than 16 days apart.
compliances.penalty: A civil penalty of no more than $25 for the second offense and every offense after it (unless the employer shows good cause), or no more than $500 for each offense if the failure results from a conspiracy between the employer and the employee.
compliances.evidence: an employer who hires an employee who resides or works in this State shall report the hiring of the employee to the state directory of new hires within twenty calendar days of the hiring of the employee
compliances.note: The state's reporting site newhire.sc.gov is a script-only application and could not be read; the deadline and penalty were read in the statute.

compliances.name: South Carolina quarterly unemployment wage report and contributions
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: South Carolina Department of Employment and Workforce
compliances.brief: Covered employers file a wage report and pay unemployment insurance tax every quarter through the SUITS system. A report is due every quarter, even with no payroll.
compliances.why: You have employees in South Carolina.
compliances.dueText: By the last day of the month following the last month of the quarter: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31.
compliances.penalty: A late filing penalty of ten percent of the contributions due for each report not filed on time; a one percent interest charge on unpaid contributions is assessed monthly; $25 for a returned payment.
compliances.evidence: By the last day of the month following the last month of the quarter, you must file your wage report and pay your taxes.

compliances.name: South Carolina unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: South Carolina Office of the State Treasurer, Unclaimed Property Program
compliances.brief: Anyone holding property that belongs to someone else and has gone unclaimed (uncashed cheques, credits, deposits, unpaid wages) reports it to the State Treasurer every year, for property as of June 30. There is no minimum amount, and the Treasurer's FAQ says a 'negative' report is filed when there is nothing to report.
compliances.why: The business holds property that belongs to someone else and has gone unclaimed.
compliances.dueText: Before November 1 each year, as of the preceding June 30. Not more than 120 days before filing, the holder sends written notice to each apparent owner whose property is worth $50 or more.
compliances.penalty: A civil penalty of $100 for each day the report is withheld, up to $5,000; a civil penalty of 25% of the value of property not paid or delivered; interest on property paid late.
compliances.evidence: The South Carolina Unclaimed Property Act requires any person who is in possession of property belonging to another; a trustee; or indebted to another on an obligation, to report unclaimed property by November 1 each year.
compliances.note: An extension may be requested before November 1 by email to the Treasurer's office.

compliances.name: South Carolina data breach notification
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: South Carolina Department of Consumer Affairs
compliances.brief: A business that owns or licenses data with personal identifying information of South Carolina residents tells the affected residents when a breach makes illegal use likely or creates a material risk of harm. If more than 1,000 people are notified at one time, it also tells the Consumer Protection Division of the Department of Consumer Affairs and the nationwide consumer reporting agencies.
compliances.why: The business holds personal information about South Carolina residents.

due.text: In the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay after discovering the breach

compliances.dueText: The law sets no number of days: the disclosure must be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay. Notice to the Department of Consumer Affairs (more than 1,000 people notified) is also without unreasonable delay.
compliances.penalty: An administrative fine of $1,000 for each resident whose information was accessible, for a knowing and wilful violation; injured residents may also sue.
compliances.evidence: The disclosure must be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, consistent with the legitimate needs of law enforcement

compliances.name: Report new hires to South Dakota
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation, New Hire Reporting Center
compliances.brief: Employers report every newly hired employee, and every rehired employee who has not been paid for the past 30 days, to the New Hire Reporting Center.
compliances.why: You have employees in South Dakota.

due.text: Within 20 days of the employee's first day of work

compliances.dueText: Newly hired or rehired employees (not paid for the past 30 days) must be reported within 20 days of the first day of work. A rehired employee is reported with the most recent date of hire.
compliances.penalty: Intentionally failing to comply is a petty offense with a penalty of $25 for each violation, and up to $500 per newly hired employee if the employer and employee conspire not to report.
compliances.evidence: Newly hired or rehired employees (employees who have not been paid for the past 30 days) must be reported to the New Hire Reporting Center within 20 days of the first day of work.

compliances.name: South Dakota quarterly reemployment assistance wage report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation, Reemployment Assistance Division
compliances.brief: South Dakota calls unemployment insurance 'reemployment assistance'. Employers file a quarterly wage report and pay the contributions due, online through the Internet Quarterly Wage Reporting System, even for a quarter with no wages.
compliances.why: You have employees in South Dakota.
compliances.dueText: Quarterly: January-March due April 30, April-June due July 31, July-September due October 31, October-December due January 31. A report is still due when no wages were paid. With prior approval, domestic employers may report annually.
compliances.penalty: $25 per month or part of a month for late filing and another $25 per month for late payment, at most $150 for any one report or contribution; interest of 1.5% per month on the tax due.
compliances.evidence: In South Dakota, wage reports are filed quarterly. Quarter | Wage Report Must Be Received By: January 1 to March 31 | April 30; April 1 to June 30 | July 31; July 1 to September 30 | October 31; October 1 to December 31 | January 31

compliances.name: South Dakota unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: South Dakota State Treasurer, Unclaimed Property Division
compliances.brief: A business holding property presumed abandoned (uncashed cheques, credits, unpaid wages and the like) reports it to the State Treasurer each year, for property as of June 30. Before filing, it tries to reach each owner and mails a notice for property worth $50 or more.
compliances.why: The business holds property that belongs to someone else and has gone unclaimed.
compliances.dueText: Before November 1 each year, as of the preceding June 30 (life insurance companies: before May 1, as of December 31). The Treasurer may postpone the date on written request.
compliances.penalty: Interest at the Category A rate on property not paid or delivered on time, from the date it should have been paid or delivered.
compliances.evidence: The report must be filed before November first of each year as of June thirtieth, next preceding, but the report of any life insurance company must be filed before May first of each year
compliances.note: The Treasurer's unclaimed property page (sdtreasurer.gov/unclaimed-property/) carries no holder deadline in its readable text; the date was read in the statute. No due-diligence day window is set: the statute says the notice is mailed before the annual report is filed.

compliances.name: South Dakota data breach notification
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: South Dakota Attorney General
compliances.brief: A business that holds personal or protected information and has a breach tells each affected South Dakota resident. If more than 250 residents are affected it also tells the Attorney General by mail or email.
compliances.why: The business holds personal information about South Dakota residents.

due.text: Within 60 days of discovering or being told of the breach

compliances.dueText: Not later than sixty days from the discovery or notification of the breach, unless law enforcement needs more time. Breaches of more than 250 residents are also disclosed to the attorney general.
compliances.penalty: The Attorney General may prosecute each failure to disclose as a deceptive act or practice and seek a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per day per violation.
compliances.evidence: A disclosure under this section shall be made not later than sixty days from the discovery or notification of the breach of system security, unless a longer period of time is required due to the legitimate needs of law enforcement

compliances.name: Report new hires to Tennessee
compliances.form: Tennessee New Hire Reporting Form or W-4
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Tennessee Department of Human Services (State Directory of New Hires)
compliances.brief: Employers report every newly hired employee, and every rehired employee who was away for at least 60 consecutive days, to the State Directory of New Hires (online at tnnewhire.com, electronically, or by mail or fax).
compliances.why: You have employees in Tennessee.

due.text: Within 20 days of the date each employee is hired

compliances.dueText: Employers must report their newly hired or rehired employees within 20 days of the date they are hired.
compliances.penalty: Failure to report a new employee could result in a fine of $20 for each employee who is not reported.
compliances.evidence: Employers must report their newly hired or rehired employees within 20 days of the date they are hired.

compliances.name: Tennessee quarterly unemployment wage report and premiums
compliances.form: Quarterly wage and premium report (Employer e-Services)
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development
compliances.brief: Employers liable for Tennessee unemployment insurance (for example, $1,500 or more of wages in a calendar quarter, or an employee in 20 different weeks of a year) file a wage report and pay premiums every quarter through Employer e-Services.
compliances.why: You have employees in Tennessee.

due.text: Each calendar quarter; confirm the due date with the Department of Labor and Workforce Development

compliances.dueText: Not confirmed: the department's page that states the quarterly due date (lwdsupport.tn.gov, 'When are quarterly reports due?') refused automated access. Confirm the date there.
compliances.evidence: An employing unit that pays $1,500 or more in total gross wages in a calendar quarter, or has at least one employee during twenty different weeks in the current or preceding calendar year regardless of the wages.
compliances.note: Who must file was read on tn.gov; the due date and late penalty were not, because lwdsupport.tn.gov returned 403. The department's FAQ PDF only says delinquent quarters can still be filed after an assessment.

compliances.name: Tennessee unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Tennessee Department of Treasury, Unclaimed Property Division
compliances.brief: Businesses holding unclaimed property (most property after 3 years of inactivity, payroll after 1 year) report and remit it to the Treasury each year through the online ReportItTN portal. Before reporting, a first-class letter goes to each owner with $50 or more.
compliances.why: The business holds property that belongs to someone else and has gone unclaimed.
compliances.dueText: Report and remit by November 1 each year. Due-diligence letters to owners of $50 or more: wait at least 60 days after mailing before reporting, and no more than 180 days.
compliances.penalty: Tennessee law provides two types of penalty: for failure to report or perform other duties, and for failure to pay or deliver property. The Treasury's pages do not state the amounts.
compliances.evidence: All Holders are required to submit an annual report by November 1st
compliances.note: For 2026 the Treasury says that because November 1 falls on a Sunday it will accept reports submitted by Monday, November 2, without penalty. The penalty amounts are only in the statute, which the Treasury links on LexisNexis and was not read.

compliances.name: Tennessee data breach notification
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Tennessee Attorney General
compliances.brief: Businesses must notify Tennessee residents whose personal information was, or may have been, acquired by an unauthorized person (Tenn. Code Ann. § 47-18-2107).
compliances.why: The business holds personal information about Tennessee residents.

due.text: Within 45 days of the breach, unless law enforcement requires an extension

compliances.dueText: In Tennessee, the organization must provide notice of the data breach within 45 days, unless law enforcement requires an extension for legitimate reasons.
compliances.evidence: In Tennessee, the organization must provide notice of the data breach within 45 days, unless law enforcement requires an extension for legitimate reasons.
compliances.note: The Attorney General's summary does not say from when the 45 days run or state a penalty; the statute itself (on LexisNexis) was not read.

compliances.name: Report new hires to Texas
compliances.form: New hire report (W-4 data, online employer portal)
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Office of the Attorney General of Texas, Child Support Division
compliances.brief: Employers report every newly hired or rehired employee who lives or works in any state (anyone who fills out a W-4) to the Texas new hire registry, online through the Attorney General's employer portal.
compliances.why: You have employees in Texas.

due.text: Within 20 calendar days from the date the employee starts earning wages

compliances.dueText: Federal and state law requires employers to report new hires and rehires within 20 calendar days from the date the employee starts earning wages.
compliances.evidence: Federal and state law requires employers to report new hires and rehires within 20 calendar days from the date the employee starts earning wages.
compliances.note: The Attorney General's page does not state a penalty.

compliances.name: Texas Employer's Quarterly Report (unemployment tax)
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Texas Workforce Commission
compliances.brief: Liable employers report each employee's gross wages every quarter and pay unemployment tax on the first $9,000 per employee per year. Reports and payments must be made electronically, and a report is due even for a quarter with no wages.
compliances.why: You have employees in Texas.
compliances.dueText: Quarterly wage reports and tax payments are due by the last day of the month following the end of the quarter: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31 (the next business day if that falls on a weekend or holiday).
compliances.penalty: Late report: $15 if filed within 15 days after the due date; after that, 0.05% of taxable wages + $30 (by the end of the following month), 0.15% + $60 (second month) or 0.35% + $90 (third month or later). Late tax: interest of 1.5% a month, up to 37.5%. Not filing and paying electronically may also be penalised.
compliances.evidence: Quarterly wage reports and tax payments are due by the last day of the month following the end of the quarter.

compliances.name: Texas unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts, Unclaimed Property Division
compliances.brief: Businesses that on March 1 hold property presumed abandoned file a report and pay it to the Comptroller by July 1, in the NAUPA electronic format. Holders that have filed before, and find nothing to report, file a negative report.
compliances.why: The business holds property that belongs to someone else and has gone unclaimed.
compliances.dueText: On or before July 1 each year, for property presumed abandoned as of March 1. Notices to owners of property worth more than $250 must be sent no later than 60 days before the report is submitted.
compliances.penalty: Interest and penalty from the date the property should have been paid until it is received; a rejected report not corrected within 30 days may be subject to a daily penalty.
compliances.evidence: Businesses (holders) who, on March 1 of each year, hold property that is presumed abandoned are required to file a report of that property on or before the following July 1.

compliances.name: Texas data breach notification
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Office of the Attorney General of Texas, Consumer Protection Division
compliances.brief: A business with a breach of system security must notify the affected consumers. If the breach affects 250 or more Texans it must also report it to the Attorney General, electronically on the OAG's Data Breach Report form.
compliances.why: The business holds personal information about Texas residents.

due.text: Attorney General report (250 or more Texans): as soon as practicably possible and no later than 30 days after discovering the breach

compliances.dueText: Report to the Attorney General as soon as practicably possible and no later than 30 days after the discovery of the breach, when 250 or more Texans are affected. Notice to affected consumers is also required.
compliances.evidence: report that breach to the Office of the Texas Attorney General as soon as practicably possible and no later than 30 days after the discovery of the breach. Businesses and organizations must also provide notice of the breach to affected consumers.
compliances.note: The Attorney General's page gives no day count for notice to consumers and no penalty; the statute (Bus. & Com. Code ch. 521) is on a script-only site that could not be read.

compliances.name: Report new hires to Utah
compliances.form: Online new hire report or Form 6
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Utah Department of Workforce Services, New Hire Registry
compliances.brief: Employers report each newly hired or rehired employee to the Utah New Hire Registry: the employee's name, Social Security number, address and date of hire, and the employer's name, FEIN and address. Online reporting is preferred.
compliances.why: You have employees in Utah.

due.text: Within 20 days of the employee's first day of work

compliances.dueText: Every employer is required to report seven mandatory data elements within 20 days of any newly hired/rehired employee's first day of work.
compliances.penalty: A civil penalty of $25 for each failure, or $500 if the failure is intentional and results from an agreement between employer and employee.
compliances.evidence: Every employer is required to report seven mandatory data elements within 20 days of any newly hired/rehired employee's first day of work.

compliances.name: Utah quarterly unemployment wage list and contribution report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Utah Department of Workforce Services, Unemployment Insurance
compliances.brief: Employers file the quarterly wage list and contribution report online and pay unemployment contributions every quarter, including quarters with no wages, until the account is closed.
compliances.why: You have employees in Utah.
compliances.dueText: Quarter ending March 31 due April 30; June 30 due July 31; September 30 due October 31; December 31 due January 31. Domestic employers may choose to file annually by January 31.
compliances.penalty: Late report: 5% of the contribution due if no more than 15 days late, plus 5% for each further 15 days, up to 25% and never less than $25. Late payment: another 5% of the contribution and interest of 1% a month. Incomplete or wrongly formatted wage information: $50 per 15 days, up to $250 per filing.
compliances.evidence: Quarter Ending: March 31 June 30 September 30 December 31 Wage Report and Contributions Due: April 30 July 31 October 31 January 31

compliances.name: Utah unclaimed property report
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Utah State Treasurer, Unclaimed Property Division
compliances.brief: A holder of property presumed abandoned files a report with the Unclaimed Property Division each year, covering the 12 months before July 1. Between 180 and 60 days before filing, it mails a notice to each owner of property worth $50 or more.
compliances.why: The business holds property that belongs to someone else and has gone unclaimed.
compliances.dueText: Before November 1 of each year, covering the 12 months preceding July 1. Owner notices: not more than 180 days nor less than 60 days before filing. An extension may be requested before the due date.
compliances.penalty: Interest at the federal short-term rate plus four percentage points, and a civil penalty of $200 for each day the duty is not performed, up to $5,000.
compliances.evidence: the report under Section 67-4a-401 shall be filed before November 1 of each year and cover the 12 months preceding July 1 of that year.
compliances.note: The Treasurer's holder FAQ (mycash.utah.gov/app/faq-report) is a script-only page and could not be read; the rule was read in the statute.

compliances.name: Utah data breach notification
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Utah Attorney General
compliances.brief: A business that owns or licenses computerized personal information of Utah residents investigates any breach promptly. If misuse for identity theft or fraud has occurred or is reasonably likely, it notifies each affected resident; for 500 or more residents also the Attorney General's office and the Utah Cyber Center; for 1,000 or more also the nationwide consumer reporting agencies.
compliances.why: The business holds personal information about Utah residents.

due.text: In the most expedient time possible without unreasonable delay

compliances.dueText: The law sets no number of days: notification is given in the most expedient time possible without unreasonable delay, after determining the scope of the breach and restoring the system's integrity.
compliances.penalty: A civil penalty of up to $2,500 for violations concerning one consumer, and up to $100,000 in total for related violations concerning more than one consumer (more in some cases).
compliances.evidence: A person required to provide notification under Subsection (1) shall provide the notification in the most expedient time possible without unreasonable delay

compliances.name: Report new hires to Virginia
compliances.form: New hire report (online, mail, phone or fax)
compliances.head: New-hire reporting
compliances.authority: Virginia Department of Social Services, Virginia New Hire Reporting Center
compliances.brief: Employers report newly hired and rehired employees (rehired after at least 60 consecutive days away), and new independent contractors, to the Virginia New Hire Reporting Center, online, by mail, phone or fax.
compliances.why: You have employees in Virginia.

due.text: Within 20 days of the employee's start date (independent contractors: within 20 days of the start of the contract)

compliances.dueText: Virginia law (§ 63.2-1946) requires all employers to report newly hired and re-hired employees and independent contractors to a state directory within 20 days of the employee's start date.
compliances.evidence: Virginia law ( § 63.2-1946 ) requires all employers to report newly hired and re-hired employees and independent contractors to a state directory within 20 days of the employee's start date.
compliances.note: Neither the DSS page nor § 63.2-1946 states a penalty.

compliances.name: Virginia quarterly unemployment tax report
compliances.head: Unemployment insurance
compliances.authority: Virginia Employment Commission
compliances.brief: Employers file the quarterly unemployment tax and wage report with the Virginia Employment Commission (through ESS, eForm or Web Upload) and pay the tax due.
compliances.why: You have employees in Virginia.
compliances.dueText: Quarterly reports are due on the last day of the following month: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31 (next business day if a weekend or holiday), by midnight of the filing deadline.
compliances.penalty: A $100 late filing penalty on each quarterly report filed after the due date (none for quarters with no wages paid); interest accrues on unpaid tax.
compliances.evidence: Quarterly reports are due on the last day of the following month. the 1st quarter ending March 31st is due April 30th

compliances.name: Virginia unclaimed property report and remittance
compliances.head: Unclaimed property
compliances.authority: Virginia Department of the Treasury, Unclaimed Property Division
compliances.brief: Holders of property presumed abandoned file a report and send the property to the Treasury each year, for the period ending June 30. At least 60 days before reporting, they try to locate each owner of property worth $100 or more.
compliances.why: The business holds property that belongs to someone else and has gone unclaimed.
compliances.dueText: Before November 1 each year for the period ending June 30 (insurance corporations: before May 1 for the period ending December 31 of the previous year). Due diligence at least 60 days before the report is submitted.
compliances.penalty: Interest at the delinquent tax rate; up to $50 per account where due diligence was not done; $100 per day a report, payment or delivery is withheld, up to the lesser of $10,000 or 25% of the property's value ($1,000 a day for wilful failure).
compliances.evidence: The report and remittance ... shall be filed before November 1 of each year for the period ending June 30 of such year, but the report and remittance of insurance corporations shall be filed before May 1 of each year

compliances.name: Virginia data breach notification
compliances.head: Data breach notification
compliances.authority: Office of the Attorney General of Virginia
compliances.brief: A business that owns or licenses computerized personal information discloses a breach to the Office of the Attorney General and to each affected Virginia resident. If more than 1,000 people are notified at once, it also tells the national consumer reporting agencies. Employers and payroll providers also tell the Attorney General about unauthorized access to income tax withholding data.
compliances.why: The business holds personal information about Virginia residents.

due.text: Without unreasonable delay after discovering the breach

compliances.dueText: The law sets no number of days: notice to the Office of the Attorney General and affected residents is given without unreasonable delay (it may be delayed to determine the scope of the breach and restore the system, or at law enforcement's request).
compliances.penalty: The Attorney General may impose a civil penalty of up to $150,000 per breach or series of similar breaches.
compliances.evidence: shall disclose any breach of the security of the system following discovery or notification of the breach of the security of the system to the Office of the Attorney General and any affected resident of the Commonwealth without unreasonable delay.

compliances.name: Enroll in RetirePath Virginia (state retirement savings programme)
compliances.head: State retirement programme
compliances.authority: Virginia College Savings Plan (Virginia529), RetirePath Virginia
